name: A name change thanks to the post office
summary: The town was first called Gilmer, but Alabama already had a Gilmer. In 1872, postmaster P. H. Kinney renamed it Hanceville to honor his father, Hance Kinney.

name: Born in a general store
summary: Hanceville voted to incorporate in May 1879, and the election was held right inside P. H. Kinney's store. Talk about shopping local!

name: The town that switched counties
summary: When Cullman County was created, the county line ran right through town. Hanceville spent years in Blount County before becoming fully part of Cullman County.

name: Hello, Hanceville Hustler
summary: From the mid 1890s until about 1908, the town had its own newspaper called The Hanceville Hustler. Best newspaper name ever? We think so.

name: Railroad roots
summary: The L&N Railroad arrived in the early 1870s, and a depot was built by 1873, helping the town grow.

name: A soda fountain older than sliced bread
summary: Hanceville Drug Co has been serving the community since 1916. Sliced bread did not show up until 1928.

name: Water since 1925
summary: The Hanceville Water and Sewer Board was established in 1925. That is a lot of sweet tea brewed with local water.

name: A library with club roots
summary: The Culture Club helped start the town library in the 1930s, and in 2022 the library moved into a building donated by Merchants Bank. The Culture Club still meets there.

name: Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrament
summary: Construction began in 1996 and the shrine was consecrated in 1999. It draws visitors and pilgrims from around the world.

name: Wallace State Community College
summary: Founded in Hanceville in 1966, Wallace State is home to the Evelyn Burrow Museum and the Burrow Center for the Fine and Performing Arts.

name: History of a Name Marker
summary: An Alabama Tourism Department marker erected in 2010 tells the story of how Hanceville got its name.

name: Ray Talley Stadium
summary: Home of the Hanceville High Bulldogs, who wear purple and gold on Friday nights.

name: Veterans Memorial Park
summary: A peaceful park with a walking trail, a pond for fishing and memorials honoring those who served.

name: How sweet is Hanceville tea?
summary: So sweet that the ice cubes ask for a dentist appointment.

name: Unsweet tea in Hanceville
summary: Ordering unsweet tea here is allowed. We just say bless your heart while we pour it.

name: Why did the tea glass go to Mud Creek?
summary: It heard there would be plenty of ice breakers.

name: Hanceville's official unit of measure
summary: One pitcher of sweet tea equals exactly one porch conversation. Two pitchers means somebody brought a pie.
